content: The frontal sinuses are located behind the superciliary arches of the forehead. These sinuses are rarely symmetrical, and the septum that separates them often deviates to one side of the midline. Each frontal sinus communicates with the anterior portion of the corresponding middle nasal meatus via the frontonasal duct. This duct passes through the anterior part of the ethmoidal labyrinth. From there, the structures open into the hiatus semilunaris within the middle nasal meatus. The mucous membrane lining the frontal sinuses is innervated by the supraorbital nerve. Blood supply to this region is provided by the supraorbital artery and the anterior ethmoidal artery. At birth, the frontal sinuses are absent. They begin to develop significantly between the ages of seven and eight years and only reach their full size after puberty.
